Semrush $139/mo, Moz $99/mo, Crunchbase $99/mo, Apollo $59/seat ... treg carries those accounts and bills you fractions of a cent per call.
take the real upstream URL you would normally call and prefix it; treg resolves the tool by host and injects the credential
base64-encode the body and add `X-Treg-Body-Encoding: base64` (also `gzip` or `base64+gzip`); treg decodes it server-side
rate that one call after using it with `treg review CALL_ID USEFULNESS [--reason "..."]` or MCP `review(call_id, usefulness, reason?)`
image and video generation (Seedance, Gemini Image, GPT Image, Seedream, Veo, Wan) and voice
A prepaid balance, metered per call at the provider's own rate, with no markup. The first $1.00 is free.
When the balance is empty, metered calls stop with a clear error until you top up. Your own-key calls keep working.
On per-success tools, a miss settles at $0.00.

A commenter found Treg's 'Clay-alternative' positioning more convincing than 'OpenRouter for agent tools', since most use cases they could think of come down to data enrichment. They otherwise called it a great product.
Legal concern: 'It's cool, but none of the T&Cs of those providers legally allow for this. There's a market for that, but heads up.'
Called it 'too good to be true': open-source and supports many free tools. Their main worry is how long the website will stay up, since some upstream providers likely won't appreciate it.

Described Treg as a set of stateless APIs that give access to data sources with one subscription, which is half of what GTM automation needs. The other half needs state (webhooks, signals, schedules), and there tools like pipe0 or Clay still have the edge.
'Useful abstraction layer for rapid prototypes, but you cannot hide upstream latency and upstream rate limits behind a single endpoint.'
One user is self-hosting Treg for development and says it can be set up and run with one click on tarvis.io.
Alternative mentioned: one commenter uses self-hosted mcp-jungle for the same purpose instead.
